limitations: A mathematical contraction valid on a zero-grade leaf is not proof of native preparability or occurrence of that same event on both inputs.
Complete scalar blindness is not physical whole-receiver blindness without the explicit identification of the scalar with the available record.
No actual accessible effect or retention-until-use is derived; an event-ordered algebraic signature is not an executable physical prediction.
Subsequent absorption of the compensating sibling erases the distinction; owner survival alone is not sufficient retention.
Occupancy-only readouts cannot distinguish the intermediate states if both are positive.
Rooted isomorphism invariance does not select the designated event; the event is a fixed addressed contraction supplied to the mathematical comparison.
